In a scratch dual workspace made by the dev binary's `init`: `commit` makes a work-repo commit
whose `ochid:` names the agent-repo's `@`, and `push` publishes that commit unchanged, the
agent-repo commit's trailer naming it back. `commit --closing` on a bookmark of two rungs makes a
merge whose parents are the fork point and the second rung, and a `jj squash` into it keeps both.

manifest's version. In this workspace, two `validate --fast` runs at different versions leave one

  bookmark: opening, the install table, the local commit, push publishing it, the closing as the
  merge, install, run-dev, closing.
  - The install table is first, so every later rung's validation installs under `tmp/dev`.
  - The commit rungs come before install and run-dev, being the larger change, and the closing as
    the merge is its own rung, so the plain commit is reviewed before the merge builds on it.

  and restore at Land, and this cycle removes only the guard, while the rule is v0.3.1's to
  change. Until Land the dev binary is `tmp/dev/bin/vc-x1-dev`, so `run-dev` is exercised by its
  tests, and the two-run check looks for that name.
- The code runs ahead of the rules, as its own cycle: the rule text names commands, so the
  commands exist before the rules do. This cycle's own rungs are pushed by the installed
  `vc-x1 0.85.5`, with `--title` and `--body`, and the next cycle runs on what this one lands.

  from the promotion, while `vc-x1 install` sees the bookmark, the remote, and the version.

  - Open: whether a failed check refuses or warns.

content.text:
Partly. The `install` subcommand as planned runs `[install] release`, the promotion to `~/.cargo/bin` at Land, and it checks that it's on pushed `main` at a bare version. So it would refuse to run mid-cycle, and it doesn't refresh `tmp/dev`.

What refreshes `tmp/dev` is the `--root tmp/dev` line in `[validate] full`, which runs before every review. So the dev binary tracks reviewed rungs whether or not `install` exists, and that's what makes it fine.

If you want a mid-cycle refresh without a full run, that's a third thing, and there are two ways to get it:
- `vc-x1 run-dev` could rebuild when the binary's `-V` doesn't match the manifest, instead of only warning. That's one extra line in its rung.
- `vc-x1 install --dev` could run the `tmp/dev` install on demand.

Neither is in the plan yet. I'd leave it out until a case shows up, since full's 8 s already covers it.

The plain version: the dev binary is kept fresh by full validation, not by the coming `install` subcommand, which is for the real install at Land.

=====
# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config::loader` finds and reads the file and returns the text with
    its path, so a caller that only wants to know which file was read
    stops there.
  - `config::parser` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands
    it a string and never touches the filesystem.
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field
    access moves behind the module boundary and the CLI no longer knows
    the file's shape.
```

The intro states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes. Each `*`
is one facet of it, each `-` under a `*` answers that facet, and nothing names a file that the
diff already lists.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". Its record is the
In Progress block in TODO.md.
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the
cycle by its title and pointing at its record. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

content.content:
### Commit-body form

The specimen is [commit-model.md](commit-model.md). A commit body is the [Problem-first
shape](#problem-first-shape) with one addition: a body whose
problem has several sub-problems arranges them by a fixed recursion, so a reader knows what any
bullet is from its marker and its depth. The earlier statement, "a problem statement then a solution
statement, both broad", left that arrangement to taste, and taste converged slowly and separately.

- **An intro paragraph states the general problem**, and defines any word the title assumes. It is
  mandatory. [Prose form](#prose-form) wants it regardless, and a body opening on a bullet is a body
  a `--body` flag can mistake for an option. The problem is *this commit's*, never the cycle's: the
  cycle's problem lives in the In Progress block, and a body whose problems outnumber what the diff
  resolves is describing something larger than the commit.
- **`*` bullets are the problem's facets**: sub-problems that decompose the intro's general problem,
  not a grab-bag of unrelated fixes. A body reaching for unrelated problem bullets is usually asking
  to be more than one commit.
- **`-` bullets are solutions**, and every `-` sits under a `*`, solving that facet. A `-` with no
  `*` above it reads as a solution to nothing, so there are no top-level solutions: a solution that
  retires every facet at once is written under each, or the facets are one.
- **One facet is the trivial commit**: the intro, one `*`, one or more `-` under it. Not a second
  form, the general form at its smallest.
- **A bookend body is a pointer**: an opening or closing commit resolves no problem of its own, so
  its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the cycle by its title and pointing at its record,
  the In Progress block. No `*`, no `-`.

**The markers are typed on purpose**: `*` always means problem, `-` always means solution, and the
pairing is what a reader counts on: the `-` answers the `*` above it, with no rule to consult. The
typing also keeps history greppable (`^\* ` finds every facet, `^ - ` every solution). Bodies are
read as plain text, in `jj log` and in terminals, where the markers survive, and if a renderer ever
flattens them the indentation still carries the structure. So the mixed markers are deliberate, and
a linter's consistent-marker rule is wrong to normalize them.

Unchanged by this: no version in title or body, no file list, no deliberation, titles per
[Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit).

### Semicolons

Prose carries no semicolons. A semicolon appears only in code (code spans, fenced code, source
files), where it is syntax rather than prose. The structure a semicolon would have joined is written
explicitly instead:

- **Two claims** take a period, each half standing as its own sentence ("The diff empties. The
  history keeps the record.").
- **A continuation** takes a comma with a conjunction, when one half carries the other's thought

content.content:
134	### Improve init and add rename and delete subcommands
135	
136	(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) A workspace's name is written into six places, and nothing renames or
137	removes them together: the work-repo's directory, the agent-repo's directory when it is not
138	nested, the two repos on the remote, each repo's `origin` URL, the `.vc-config.{toml|md}` of both
139	sides, and the Claude Code symlink. And `init` makes a workspace it cannot always finish, or that
140	Claude Code does not find.
141	
142	- The order is wink's: `init` is fixed first, then `vc-x1 delete`, then `vc-x1 rename`. Each is a
143	  cycle of its own.
144	- The `init` work is more than one cycle, wink's order: the agent template `--use-template` looks
145	  for first, then the path over 200 characters, then the name GitHub would change, the order the
146	  three parts below are in.
147	- Delete is ahead of rename: its "find every part of a workspace from its config" is what rename
148	  reuses, and it gives `init` the cleanup it lacks.
149	- The parts are `####` headings, where [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format) asks for
150	  bullets with a bold title, since a heading is an anchor a link can name.
151	- Delete leans on two entries far down this list: the clean verdict of [status prints a verdict
152	  per repo and exits with a bit per
153	  side](#status-prints-a-verdict-per-repo-and-exits-with-a-bit-per-side), and [status reports the
154	  commits no bookmark reaches](#status-reports-the-commits-no-bookmark-reaches). Whether they move
155	  up ahead of it, or delete's cycle builds the verdict as its first rung, is open.
156	- One experiment wants wink starting a fresh Claude Code session, the symlink's below.
157	
158	#### init --use-template takes an existing workspace as the template
159	
160	(wink, 2026-10-09) Someday an existing work directory should serve as a template. Today
161	`--use-template WORK` requires an agent template too, defaulting to the sibling directory
162	`<WORK>.claude`, and a workspace has no such sibling: its agent-repo is nested inside it and holds
163	session data, which is nothing to copy.
164	
165	```
166	$ vc-x1 init io-uring-2-zcr-v4-x2 --use-template io_uring-2-zcr-v4-x1/
167	vc-x1 0.84.15
168	Preflight checks...
169	error: --use-template: agent template 'io_uring-2-zcr-v4-x1.claude' does not exist
170	```
171	
172	Met again 2026-10-11 at 0.84.21, the same command and the same error, the template a workspace
173	whose agent-repo is the nested `.agent-session`.
174	
175	- The agent template becomes optional: the sibling when it exists, otherwise an agent-repo seeded
176	  with nothing.
177	- The sibling default still ends in `.claude`, and whether it follows the `.agent-session` rename
178	  is decided with the template repo, where the short-term fix, updating its `work` and
179	  `work.claude`, is being made.
180	
181	#### symlink names a path over 200 characters as Claude Code does
182	
183	(2026-10-09) Claude Code cuts a project name longer than 200 characters to 200 and appends `-` and
184	a base-36 hash of the path, and `encode_path` returns the uncut name, so `vc-x1 symlink` makes a
185	link Claude Code never reads for such a path. Found in the installed Claude Code (2.1.295) during
186	the cycle "fix: symlink names a project as Claude Code does", which left it out: the hash function
187	has to be copied exactly, and no path met so far is near 200.
188	
189	Whether the hash has to match bit for bit is not known, and the opening tests it before any code is
190	written. On a scratch project whose full path is over 200 characters, wink starting a fresh Claude
191	Code session there for each pass:
192	
193	- No link: the name Claude Code creates under `~/.claude/projects` is the ground truth, and a test
194	  vector for the hash if one is needed.
195	- The link as `vc-x1 symlink` makes it today, the uncut name: expected to be ignored, Claude Code
196	  creating its own directory beside it as it did for the `io_uring` project, whose link was wrong
197	  within the first 200 characters.
198	- A link made by hand, the first 200 characters and a made-up suffix: used or ignored, and this
199	  pass decides the design.
200	  - Used: the fix is the cut and a fixed suffix, with no hash to copy.
201	  - Ignored: the hash is reproduced exactly, and the first pass's name is its test.
202	
203	We think the third pass may be used: Claude Code's hash is recalled, not read this session, as
204	differing between its native and Node installs, with a match on the first 200 characters as the
205	fallback.
206	
207	#### init refuses a name GitHub would change
208	
209	(wink + agent, 2026-10-09) GitHub allows letters, digits, `.`, `-`, and `_` in a repo name and
210	turns any other character into `-` without saying so. `init` asks for the repo under the name as
211	typed and pushes to the URL built from that name, which does not exist when GitHub changed it:
212	
213	```
214	$ vc-x1 init test_underscore=equal+plus-dash__two-unscores
215	vc-x1 0.84.18
216	...
217	Step 8: Set main on the agent repo's initial commit, create GitHub repo winksaville/test_underscore=equal+plus-dash__two-unscores.agent-session --public, and push to https://github.com/winksaville/test_underscore=equal+plus-dash__two-unscores.agent-session.git
218	error: failed after 5 attempts: Git process failed: External git program failed:
219	fatal: repository 'https://github.com/winksaville/test_underscore=equal+plus-dash__two-unscores.agent-session.git/' not found
220	```
221	
222	GitHub had created `test_underscore-equal-plus-dash__two-unscores.agent-session`, so the run left
223	an empty public repo there and a local workspace with no remote.
224	
225	- Preflight refuses such a name when the target provisions a GitHub repo, and says what GitHub
226	  would make of it. `github_slug` already refuses a name ending in `.git`, and this check sits
227	  beside it.
228	- No silent rename: taking GitHub's version of the name would work, and the directory and the
229	  remote would then carry different names nobody chose.
230	- A local-only name is left alone, since the name is a fine directory.
231	- A push that fails with "not found" is not retried, as the five attempts here were.
232	- `init` has no undo, so a late failure leaves the earlier steps' work behind. The preflight check
233	  avoids this case and not the general one, which is its own entry if it is wanted.
234	
235	#### delete removes a workspace from this machine
236	
237	- It removes the directories and the symlink, and leaves the remote alone. A repo on the remote
238	  is deleted by hand.
239	- Its prompt lists what goes and the commits that are nowhere else.
240	- What stops it is below.
241	
242	#### rename renames a workspace, its remote included
243	
244	- It renames the repos on the remote too. The remote cannot be lost by it: the remote's rename
245	  happens or is refused, so the repo is under the old name or the new one.
246	- The remote goes first, so a refusal (the name taken, no permission) leaves the local side as it
247	  was. The order after it: both `origin` URLs, the configs, a commit and push in both repos, the
248	  directory, the symlink.
249	- The new name is checked as [init refuses a name GitHub would
250	  change](#init-refuses-a-name-github-would-change) checks one, so the URL written is the name
251	  the remote took.
252	- A run that stopped between the two repos is run again: it finds which repo has the new name
253	  and goes on from there.
254	- A workspace with no remote skips the remote steps. A remote that is not GitHub's is refused.
255	- Left out, and listed by the command: the name as the family's other repos hold it, the
256	  template, the messages, and the other members' configs.
257	- Open: whether it takes the workspace whole or one side at a time. One side alone overlaps
258	  [repos.agent becomes repos.agent-dir, and a command brings a config up to
259	  date](#reposagent-becomes-reposagent-dir-and-a-command-brings-a-config-up-to-date).
260	- Open: whether `.vc-config.toml` is still a form the commands handle.
261	
262	#### What stops delete and rename

### Improve init and add rename and delete subcommands

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) A workspace's name is written into six places, and nothing renames or
removes them together: the work-repo's directory, the agent-repo's directory when it is not
nested, the two repos on the remote, each repo's `origin` URL, the `.vc-config.{toml|md}` of both
sides, and the Claude Code symlink. And `init` makes a workspace it cannot always finish, or that
Claude Code does not find.

- The order is wink's: `init` is fixed first, then `vc-x1 delete`, then `vc-x1 rename`. Each is a
  cycle of its own.
- The `init` work is more than one cycle, wink's order: the agent template `--use-template` looks
  for first, then the path over 200 characters, then the name GitHub would change, the order the
  three parts below are in.
- Delete is ahead of rename: its "find every part of a workspace from its config" is what rename
  reuses, and it gives `init` the cleanup it lacks.
- The parts are `####` headings, where [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format) asks for
  bullets with a bold title, since a heading is an anchor a link can name.
- Delete leans on two entries far down this list: the clean verdict of [status prints a verdict
  per repo and exits with a bit per
  side](#status-prints-a-verdict-per-repo-and-exits-with-a-bit-per-side), and [status reports the
  commits no bookmark reaches](#status-reports-the-commits-no-bookmark-reaches). Whether they move
  up ahead of it, or delete's cycle builds the verdict as its first rung, is open.
- One experiment wants wink starting a fresh Claude Code session, the symlink's below.

#### init --use-template takes an existing workspace as the template

(wink, 2026-10-09) Someday an existing work directory should serve as a template. Today
`--use-template WORK` requires an agent template too, defaulting to the sibling directory
`<WORK>.claude`, and a workspace has no such sibling: its agent-repo is nested inside it and holds
session data, which is nothing to copy.

```
$ vc-x1 init io-uring-2-zcr-v4-x2 --use-template io_uring-2-zcr-v4-x1/
vc-x1 0.84.15
Preflight checks...
error: --use-template: agent template 'io_uring-2-zcr-v4-x1.claude' does not exist
```

Met again 2026-10-11 at 0.84.21, the same command and the same error, the template a workspace
whose agent-repo is the nested `.agent-session`.

- The agent template becomes optional: the sibling when it exists, otherwise an agent-repo seeded
  with nothing.
- The sibling default still ends in `.claude`, and whether it follows the `.agent-session` rename
  is decided with the template repo, where the short-term fix, updating its `work` and
  `work.claude`, is being made.

#### symlink names a path over 200 characters as Claude Code does

(2026-10-09) Claude Code cuts a project name longer than 200 characters to 200 and appends `-` and
a base-36 hash of the path, and `encode_path` returns the uncut name, so `vc-x1 symlink` makes a
link Claude Code never reads for such a path. Found in the installed Claude Code (2.1.295) during
the cycle "fix: symlink names a project as Claude Code does", which left it out: the hash function
has to be copied exactly, and no path met so far is near 200.

Whether the hash has to match bit for bit is not known, and the opening tests it before any code is
written. On a scratch project whose full path is over 200 characters, wink starting a fresh Claude
Code session there for each pass:

- No link: the name Claude Code creates under `~/.claude/projects` is the ground truth, and a test
  vector for the hash if one is needed.
- The link as `vc-x1 symlink` makes it today, the uncut name: expected to be ignored, Claude Code
  creating its own directory beside it as it did for the `io_uring` project, whose link was wrong
  within the first 200 characters.
- A link made by hand, the first 200 characters and a made-up suffix: used or ignored, and this
  pass decides the design.
  - Used: the fix is the cut and a fixed suffix, with no hash to copy.
  - Ignored: the hash is reproduced exactly, and the first pass's name is its test.

We think the third pass may be used: Claude Code's hash is recalled, not read this session, as
differing between its native and Node installs, with a match on the first 200 characters as the
fallback.

#### init refuses a name GitHub would change

(wink + agent, 2026-10-09) GitHub allows letters, digits, `.`, `-`, and `_` in a repo name and
turns any other character into `-` without saying so. `init` asks for the repo under the name as
typed and pushes to the URL built from that name, which does not exist when GitHub changed it:

```
$ vc-x1 init test_underscore=equal+plus-dash__two-unscores
vc-x1 0.84.18
...
Step 8: Set main on the agent repo's initial commit, create GitHub repo winksaville/test_underscore=equal+plus-dash__two-unscores.agent-session --public, and push to https://github.com/winksaville/test_underscore=equal+plus-dash__two-unscores.agent-session.git
error: failed after 5 attempts: Git process failed: External git program failed:
fatal: repository 'https://github.com/winksaville/test_underscore=equal+plus-dash__two-unscores.agent-session.git/' not found
```

GitHub had created `test_underscore-equal-plus-dash__two-unscores.agent-session`, so the run left
an empty public repo there and a local workspace with no remote.

- Preflight refuses such a name when the target provisions a GitHub repo, and says what GitHub
  would make of it. `github_slug` already refuses a name ending in `.git`, and this check sits
  beside it.
- No silent rename: taking GitHub's version of the name would work, and the directory and the
  remote would then carry different names nobody chose.
- A local-only name is left alone, since the name is a fine directory.
- A push that fails with "not found" is not retried, as the five attempts here were.
- `init` has no undo, so a late failure leaves the earlier steps' work behind. The preflight check
  avoids this case and not the general one, which is its own entry if it is wanted.

#### delete removes a workspace from this machine

- It removes the directories and the symlink, and leaves the remote alone. A repo on the remote
  is deleted by hand.
- Its prompt lists what goes and the commits that are nowhere else.
- What stops it is below.

#### rename renames a workspace, its remote included

- It renames the repos on the remote too. The remote cannot be lost by it: the remote's rename
  happens or is refused, so the repo is under the old name or the new one.
- The remote goes first, so a refusal (the name taken, no permission) leaves the local side as it
  was. The order after it: both `origin` URLs, the configs, a commit and push in both repos, the
  directory, the symlink.
- The new name is checked as [init refuses a name GitHub would
  change](#init-refuses-a-name-github-would-change) checks one, so the URL written is the name
  the remote took.
- A run that stopped between the two repos is run again: it finds which repo has the new name
  and goes on from there.
- A workspace with no remote skips the remote steps. A remote that is not GitHub's is refused.
- Left out, and listed by the command: the name as the family's other repos hold it, the
  template, the messages, and the other members' configs.
- Open: whether it takes the workspace whole or one side at a time. One side alone overlaps
  [repos.agent becomes repos.agent-dir, and a command brings a config up to
  date](#reposagent-becomes-reposagent-dir-and-a-command-brings-a-config-up-to-date).
- Open: whether `.vc-config.toml` is still a form the commands handle.

#### What stops delete and rename

- An agent running in the workspace is not looked for. No lock is asked for, the session's being
  off and the one `vc-x1` was to take for a run not added ([vc-x1 takes a lock of its own for a
  run that writes](notes/todo-backlog.md#vc-x1-takes-a-lock-of-its-own-for-a-run-that-writes)).
- Uncommitted work, or unpushed work on a bookmark, refuses. This is the status verdict, called
  and not written again. The agent-repo's `@` is clean only after the session exits and a
  `squash-push`.
- Two findings warn and need a yes, `--yes` on the command line or `Y` at the prompt, an agent
  with no terminal using the flag as it does for push:
  - Commits no bookmark reaches.
  - A half-made workspace, a repo with no remote at all, as an `init` that failed before
    publishing leaves. Everything in it is unpushed, and it is the cleanup delete is wanted for.
- We think the two warnings are delete's alone: such commits move with the directory in a rename.

My recommendation is no, keep it separate and run it after this cycle lands. The reasons:

- **The entry already says it's several cycles.** "Each is a cycle of its own" is your order from 2026-10-11, and the `init` part alone is "more than one cycle". It has five parts, one of which, the 200-character symlink, waits on you starting fresh Claude Code sessions for its experiment, and `delete` leans on two `status` entries far down the list.
- **One problem per cycle.** This cycle's record, bookmark, and title are about the review-to-publish gap. Rename and delete share nothing with it beyond being Rust in `src/`, and that's true of every feature. The commit-body rule says a body reaching for unrelated problem bullets is asking to be more than one commit, and the same holds for a cycle: the closing would describe two unrelated things, and `git log --grep` on either title would find the other's rungs.
- **Size.** Eight rungs is already more than the last cycle managed, which closed as a dead end at nine.
- **Order helps.** With this cycle landed first, the `init`, `delete`, and `rename` cycles are the first to run under `vc-x1 commit`, `install --dev`, and the trapezoid made at commit time. That's the dogfooding you asked for, on real work rather than on the cycle that builds the tools.
